# Remendra

Persistent memory extension for Pi. Stores structured claims with source evidence in SQLite, provides FTS5 recall, and injects query-matched context into each agent turn.

Version: 2.0.0-alpha.2
Runtime: Pi 0.85.1, Node 24
Storage: SQLite + FTS5 in a worker thread
License: MIT

## Install

pi install git:github.com/yoda-digital/pi-remendra

## Commands

/remendra help — list all commands
/remendra search <query> — find memories
/remendra remember <JSON> — record a fact, decision, constraint, or procedure
/remendra correct <id> <JSON> — replace a memory with transactional correction
/remendra why <id> — show sources, revisions, and dependents
/remendra settings — view or change configuration

## How it works

1. New session entries are ingested as source records with SHA-256 content hashes.
2. After the agent settles, an observer model extracts structured claims from unprocessed source chunks. Each claim carries evidence: exact character spans into the stored source text.
3. Before each agent turn, Remendra compiles a memory packet. FTS5 matches the current query. Results are ranked by search score and claim-type priority.
4. Corrections are transactional: the old claim is superseded, dependents are invalidated recursively, the replacement is recorded with its own evidence.

Memories default to lineage scope (current session branch). Promote to project or user scope explicitly.

## Configuration

Default storage: ~/.pi/agent/pi-remendra/v2/
Override: PI_REMENDRA_HOME
Disable: PI_REMENDRA_PASSIVE=true

Daily token budget: 80,000 (configurable)
Token estimation: ceil(UTF-8 bytes / 3) — heuristic, not exact

See example-config.json for the full defaults.
